title: Bliss - Durable Service Marketplace
subtitle: Java 21, Quarkus, PostgreSQL, Keycloak, and Flutter marketplace for service requests, quotes, bookings, chat, reviews, and disputes.
summary: Cross-platform service marketplace with durable booking and dispute workflows, provider operations, participant-only messaging, simulated payments, and verified web and mobile flows.
description: Bliss is a two-sided marketplace where customers request or directly book local services and providers manage offerings, send quotes, complete work, and communicate through the booking lifecycle. The preserved prototype was rebuilt as a Java 21 and Quarkus modular monolith with PostgreSQL, Keycloak authentication, durable Quarkus Flow orchestration, and a Flutter client verified across web, Android, and an iOS simulator.
highlights: Rebuilt the original prototype into a modular Quarkus backend and Flutter client with public discovery, provider onboarding, and owned service management.
Implemented customer requests, provider quotes, direct bookings, protected booking actions, and stale-price and duplicate-submission safeguards.
Used durable BookingLifecycleFlow and DisputeFlow workflows for human wait states, deadlines, retries, compensation, and idempotent simulated settlement.
Added participant-only booking chat, bounded message pagination, safe send retries, completed-booking reviews, and dispute evidence with admin decisions.
Verified request-to-review flows on web, Android, and an iOS simulator, with backend, Flutter, process-restart, and CI coverage.
Added an isolated PostgreSQL backup and restore rehearsal plus an operational recovery runbook without exposing real user data.
note: Bliss currently runs as a local project with simulated payments only; no real money moves. Web, Android, and iOS simulator request-to-review flows are verified, while secondary iOS acceptance remains open.

title: ServiceDesk Automatization
subtitle: Local-first Windows diagnostics desktop app built with Electron, React, TypeScript, FastAPI, and Python.
summary: Consent-driven workstation diagnostics with deterministic issue detection, guided remediation, restart-safe report history, privacy-controlled exports, and an allowlisted DNS repair flow.
description: ServiceDesk Automatization is a local-first Windows desktop application designed to turn system diagnostics into clear, reviewable support workflows. It collects a limited set of event logs and system snapshots after explicit consent, identifies common workstation issues, presents guided checks, and keeps report and repair history on the device.
highlights: Built an Electron and React desktop interface backed by a FastAPI and Python collector that stays on the local Windows machine.
Added explicit consent before reading recent event logs, CPU, memory, disk, uptime, process, and Wi-Fi snapshots.
Implemented deterministic detection for application crashes, service failures, low disk space, DNS and network problems, Windows Update, drivers, and Wi-Fi health.
Created restart-safe report history with retention controls, semantic comparisons, deletion, and privacy-controlled JSON and PDF exports.
Designed an allowlisted DNS cache repair with disclosure, one-time approval, native confirmation, timeout handling, verification, recovery, and a redacted audit record.
Added automated frontend and backend checks plus packaged Windows alpha and installer acceptance documentation.
note: This is an internal Windows alpha with no cloud account, synchronization, analysis, or telemetry path. Portfolio screenshots use the project's documented diagnostic fixture data.

title: VenueOps - Event Operations Platform
subtitle: ASP.NET Core 8, React, and PostgreSQL platform for venue bookings, staff assignments, guest counts, shift notes, and role-based dashboards.
summary: Production-style event operations application inspired by real hospitality workflows, with authentication, staffing, booking management, demo data, Docker setup, CI, and Render deployment.
description: VenueOps is a full-stack event operations platform built to show how software can support real venue and hospitality workflows. The application covers venue bookings, client and room management, staff assignments, guest counts, shift notes, role-aware dashboards, demo accounts, public documentation, Docker Compose local setup, and a live Render deployment.
highlights: Designed a relational data model for users, clients, venue rooms, event bookings, staff assignments, and shift notes.
Implemented JWT authentication with BCrypt password hashing and role-based access for Admin, Manager, Staff, and Demo users.
Built responsive React workflows for booking CRUD, staffing, status updates, dashboard metrics, and shift note capture.
Added automated backend and frontend tests plus GitHub Actions CI for build, test, and Docker image validation.
Published a live demo with seeded demo data, Docker Compose local setup, architecture documentation, and public project assets.
note: The public demo uses seeded demo data on Render. The project documentation describes local Docker Compose as the strongest guaranteed demo path.

title: PokeBot Gen 3 - Autonomous Emerald Extension
subtitle: Python automation, persisted campaign control, and a React telemetry dashboard extending the open-source Pokebot Gen 3 project.
summary: Open-source engineering work that extends autonomous Pokemon Emerald progression through Hall of Fame checkpoints with recovery, integrity guardrails, SQLite state, and live observer telemetry.
description: This project is a fork of 40Cakes/pokebot-gen3 that Lucas extended toward autonomous Pokemon Emerald story completion and guarded post-game collection. The work adds campaign lifecycle control, restart-safe checkpoints, navigation and battle preparation, persistent telemetry, and a browser observer dashboard while preserving the upstream project's normal-controller-input integrity model.
highlights: Extended the autonomous Emerald story path through eight badges, HM traversal, party preparation, the Elite Four, Wallace, and a durable Hall of Fame checkpoint.
Added persisted campaign lifecycle controls and restart recovery so long-running automation can resume from verified checkpoints.
Built a React and Vite observer dashboard with REST startup state, WebSocket telemetry, world position, party status, runtime events, and operator lifecycle controls.
Used SQLite-backed state and source and input fingerprints to keep campaign evidence and continuation decisions auditable.
Added bounded post-game collection workflows with protected specimen identities and fail-closed safety checks.
Kept the integrity boundary explicit: observe game memory and send normal controller input without distributing ROMs, saves, or BIOS files, or injecting items and event flags.
note: This is a GPL-3.0 open-source fork of 40Cakes/pokebot-gen3. M3 checkpoint 10 and Hall of Fame completion from prepared checkpoints are verified; an uninterrupted fresh-save acceptance run remains pending. Users must supply their own legal game files.

title: StockPilot - Smart Inventory Management System
subtitle: ASP.NET Core MVC inventory management platform with PostgreSQL, role-based access, stock tracking, dashboard analytics, and Render deployment.
summary: Full-stack inventory management web application for small business operations with products, categories, suppliers, stock tracking, orders, user roles, and dashboard metrics.
description: StockPilot was built as a full-stack inventory management system focused on practical business workflows. The application supports product and supplier management, dashboard analytics, low-stock monitoring, stock movement history, order workflows, role-based access, and deployed demo access backed by PostgreSQL.
highlights: Built role-based authentication and authorization with ASP.NET Core Identity for Admin, Manager, and Staff workflows.
Designed PostgreSQL data models and EF Core relationships for products, categories, suppliers, orders, order items, stock movements, and audit logs.
Implemented product search, category and supplier filters, stock status filters, sorting, and pagination.
Added dashboard metrics for inventory value, potential revenue, low-stock items, out-of-stock items, recent movements, and recent orders.
Implemented stock movement tracking so inventory changes are recorded instead of only updating final quantity.
Deployed the application on Render with PostgreSQL and documented the project with screenshots, demo accounts, and setup steps.
note: The Render PostgreSQL demo database is on a free plan and may expire or reset over time.

title: Hair Stylist Booking Web Application
subtitle: Booking, portfolio, testimonial, admin, and mobile-ready product direction for a Toronto hairstylist business.
summary: Team-built booking platform for a hairstylist business with client scheduling, digital portfolio support, admin workflows, and matching web and mobile product planning.
description: This project was created to improve how a hairstylist manages appointments, availability, and digital presence. The product direction combines client booking, account-based scheduling, admin workflow support, portfolio and testimonial presentation, and a matching mobile experience for the broader service flow.
highlights: Planned and implemented a booking system focused on available time slots, rescheduling, and cancellation support.
Included admin workflow support for schedule management, appointment updates, and customer records.
Designed the product around both customer booking needs and a hairstylist workflow that reduces manual coordination.
Covered portfolio and testimonial presentation so the product also supports digital presence beyond scheduling.
Extended the product direction across web, backend API, and mobile prototype work.
note: This project is shown as portfolio case study material rather than a public demo.
